title: Using AI Safely
intro: Learn what never to type into a chatbot, how to use placeholders, and how to stay honest about when AI helped.
recap: Treat a chatbot like a stranger's notebook. Do not write private things in it.
Never type passwords, OTPs, PINs, card or ID numbers, or other people's private details.
Use placeholders such as [Name] and add the real details yourself afterwards.
Follow your school's or workplace's rules, and say when AI helped.

screens.title: What You Type May Be Kept

aiTutor.recap: Treat a chatbot like a stranger's notebook: do not write private things in it. How a tool handles what you type depends on the tool and its settings, so the safe rule is to type only what you would share with a stranger.
aiTutor.example: Before pasting a draft email into a chatbot, you replace your account number and your colleague's name with placeholders. You still get the help, and nothing private leaves your phone.
aiTutor.watchOut: A friendly, private-feeling chat window makes it easy to over-share. It is still a company's computer on the other end.
aiTutor.tryThis: Look at the settings or help page of the chatbot you use most and find what it says about storing your chats.

glossary.definition: Kept somewhere so it can be used later. A chatbot company may keep what you type, depending on the tool and its settings.
glossary.example: A message you typed last week may still be on a company's computers today.

glossary.definition: Telling the truth about your own work, including when a tool helped you write it.
glossary.example: Handing in an essay written by a chatbot as if you wrote it yourself, when the rules forbid it, is not honest.

glossary.definition: The ability to weigh a situation and decide well. Judgement stays with you; a chatbot can offer ideas but should not make serious choices for you.
glossary.example: A chatbot can list the pros and cons of a loan. Deciding whether to take it is yours to do.

paragraphs: When you type into an AI chatbot, your words go to a company's computers. Depending on the tool and its settings, they may be stored, read by staff, or used to improve the system. You usually cannot take them back.
So the safe rule is to type only what you would be comfortable sharing with a stranger. That keeps you safe even if you are not sure how a tool handles your data.
Safe use is also about honesty and judgement: telling people when AI helped, and not letting it make serious decisions for you.

aiTutor.explain: Decide whether each statement is true or false. Imagine reading it aloud to a stranger. If you would not say it to them, do not type it to a chatbot.
aiTutor.tryThis: For each card, ask: what is the worst thing that could happen if this text ended up in the wrong hands?

widgetData.instruction: Is each statement true or false?

cards.statement: It is fine to paste your banking password so the chatbot can help you log in.
cards.explanation: Passwords, PINs and OTPs are for you alone. No chatbot needs them to help, and sharing one is a risk.
cards.bonusFact: If you ever typed a password or code by mistake, change it straight away.

cards.statement: You can ask for help writing a CV without including your ID number, home address or bank details.
cards.explanation: Useful help rarely needs private identifiers. You can add them later in your own document.
cards.bonusFact: Write the CV with placeholders, then add your own details in your own copy.

cards.statement: A friend's private message is safe to paste in, because it is only a chat.
cards.explanation: Other people's private details are not yours to share. Remove names and personal details first.
cards.bonusFact: Remove names and personal details before you paste, or describe the situation in your own words.

cards.statement: Your employer's confidential files are fine to paste in if the chatbot is free.
cards.explanation: Being free does not make it private. Check your workplace rules before putting work documents into any tool.
cards.bonusFact: Read your workplace's rules, or ask your manager, before you paste work files into any AI tool.

aiTutor.explain: Think about which version still lets the chatbot help, without any private identifiers. The best prompt keeps the job and removes the names, numbers and addresses.
aiTutor.watchOut: A document full of details is often pasted "to save time". Typing a short description of the situation is usually safer and works just as well.

widgetData.question: You want help writing a complaint to your landlord. Which prompt is the safest?

options.text: "My name is [full name], ID [number], I live at [full address]. Write a complaint about the broken water pipe."
"Write a polite, firm complaint to my landlord about a broken water pipe that has not been fixed for two weeks. Leave the names blank."
"Here is my tenancy agreement with all my details. Write a complaint."

widgetData.explanation: It gives the tool everything it needs and leaves the names and details out. You can fill them in afterwards on your own copy, where nobody else sees them.
widgetData.bonusFact: Using placeholders such as [Name] is an easy habit that keeps private details out of the chat. Replace them yourself when you copy the result.

aiTutor.explain: Tap each card for one habit that keeps you safe. Together they cover what you share, what you trust, and what you say about your own work.
aiTutor.example: Before using a chatbot for a school essay, you check your school's rules, leave out personal details, verify any facts it gives, and say that you used it if the rules ask you to.
aiTutor.tryThis: Write the three words protect, check, be honest on a note, and use them the next time you open a chatbot.

nodes.label: Protect
nodes.title: Protect private data
nodes.definition: Never type passwords, OTPs, PINs, card or ID numbers. Leave out other people's private details. Use placeholders for names.
nodes.bonusFact: If you ever typed a secret by mistake, change it straight away.

nodes.label: Check
nodes.title: Check before you act
nodes.definition: Verify important facts, and do not let a chatbot make decisions about health, law or money alone. Look at the tool's privacy settings and choose the most private option available.
nodes.bonusFact: Settings differ between tools, so look at yours rather than assuming.

nodes.label: Be honest
nodes.title: Be honest about using it
nodes.definition: If a school, employer or client expects your own work, follow their rules and say when AI helped. Do not pass off a chatbot's text as something you wrote when that is not allowed.
nodes.bonusFact: Your own thinking is the part of the work that cannot be copied, so keep doing it.

widgetData.completionMessage: You have the three safety habits: protect, check and be honest.
widgetData.completionBonusFact: These same habits protect you whichever AI tool you use, today or in the future. Tools change; the habits do not.

screens.title: Match the Risk to the Habit

aiTutor.review: Match each risk to the habit that protects you. Each habit closes one of the main ways AI use can go wrong.
aiTutor.watchOut: Do not let one habit stand in for the others. A prompt with no private data can still contain a wrong fact, and a checked fact can still be dishonestly passed off as your own work.

widgetData.instruction: Match each risk to the habit that protects you:

pairs.left: Pasting an OTP into a chat
Acting on a medicine answer alone
Handing in AI text as your own
pairs.right: Follow the rules and say so

widgetData.explanation: Each habit closes one of the main ways AI use can hurt you or other people.

aiTutor.review: One last sentence to finish the course. It ties the three lessons together: ask clearly, check what comes back, and keep secrets out.
aiTutor.tryThis: Pick one habit from this course and try it for a week.

widgetData.template: Ask clearly, {blank} the answer, and never type secrets.
widgetData.explanation: These three habits cover the course: ask with context and a goal, check what comes back, and keep private data out. Together they make a chatbot a safe, useful helper.
widgetData.bonusFact: Teaching one friend what you learned here is a great way to remember it, and it spreads safer habits to someone you care about.
